questions.question: In which accidents does the narrative say the pilot or flight instructor tried to get the engine running again after it stopped producing power in flight, but could not?

chunks.quote: attempted to restart the engine with no success
made multiple attempts to restart the engine, which were unsuccessful
attempts to restore fuel flow and restart the engine were unsuccessful
attempted to restore engine power by switching to the right fuel tank and activating the starter but was unsuccessful

questions.note: Four accidents, each worded differently and none with the question's idea words 'tried', 'running again', 'stopped producing' or 'could not' (the noun 'engine' is shared by every passage as the thing restarted, not as a wording of the idea): CEN21LA414 (LaSalle, CO: the flight instructor 'attempted to restart the engine with no success'), CEN22LA194 (Traverse City, MI: 'multiple attempts to restart the engine, which were unsuccessful'), CEN22LA059 (Cleveland, TX: 'attempts to restore fuel flow and restart the engine were unsuccessful') and CEN23LA344 (Oberlin, KS: the restart is described, not named: the pilot 'attempted to restore engine power by switching to the right fuel tank and activating the starter but was unsuccessful'). All four are total losses of engine power, which is why the question says 'stopped producing power' rather than 'lost power'. Lookalikes that must not count: CEN21LA362 (Topeka, KS), where the engine only partly lost power and kept running and the pilot 'tried to advance the power forward with no change', not a restart; CEN21LA173 (Dustin, OK), where the helicopter pilot 'attempted to regain rotor rpm but was unsuccessful' with an engine that never stopped; CEN23LA223 (Lake Village, AR), where the airplane 'lost thrust, but the engine remained operating' and no attempt is described; CEN21LA383 (Gypsum, CO), where the engine 'regained power briefly' on its own after the pilot leveled off, before going to idle, and no restart attempt is described; and the post-accident engine test runs of CEN21LA382 and CEN22LA059, made on the ground after the accident and successful. The other power-loss accidents (CEN21LA221, CEN21LA382, CEN21LA284, CEN23LA017, CEN22LA312) describe no attempt to restart. The events_sequence and findings tables code the loss of power, not the restart attempt.

questions.question: In which accidents does the narrative describe an unusual noise that the pilot heard from the aircraft before the accident (a warning horn does not count)?

chunks.quote: a “very loud pop” noise emitted from behind the instrument panel
the pilot heard a “pop” and observed white smoke trailing the airplane
he heard a slight noise that originated from the front of the airplane
the engine made a “coughing” sound and lost power

questions.note: Four accidents: CEN21LA268 (Saint James, LA: a 'very loud pop' noise from behind the instrument panel, the failed air-conditioning hose), CEN22LA312 (Decatur, IL: the pilot heard a 'pop' during climbout, the fractured turbine blades), CEN22LA244 (Salina, KS: a slight noise from the front of the airplane while taxiing, then a louder one on the takeoff roll) and CEN23LA017 (Loveland, CO), whose passage shares no key word with the question (not 'heard', 'noise', 'unusual', 'pilot' or 'aircraft'): the engine 'made a coughing sound and lost power' during the go-around. The question says 'aircraft' on purpose: 'airplane' and 'engine' appear in the qualifying passages. Lookalikes that must not count: the warning horns, excluded by name in the question, of ANC21LA079 (Pelican, AK: the low rotor rpm 'horn sounded') and CEN21LA185 (Schaumburg, IL: 'the stall warning horn came on'), plus the stall warning of CEN22LA249; CEN21FA299 (Lamoni, IA), where witnesses, not the pilot, 'heard an increase in engine power', the normal sound of a go-around; CEN22LA310 (Wyoming, IL), where the pilot 'heard the engine spool up' (normal) and 'heard it contact the corn' (the accident itself, not a sound before it); CEN21LA383 (Gypsum, CO), where the engine 'ran rough', a behaviour, with no noise described; CEN21LA221 (Pinckneyville, IL), where the engine 'began to shake', felt, not heard; and CEN21LA339 (West Liberty, IA), where the pilot felt a 'big tug' and a 'huge jerk'. CEN21LA268 does not use the verb 'heard' but the pilot reported the noise himself. No finding or occurrence code records a noise.

questions.question: Among the Air Tractor AT-502B accidents, in which does the narrative say the pilot made a forced landing?

chunks.quote: The pilot performed a forced landing to a bean field.
The pilot made a forced landing
completed a forced landing to a field

questions.note: Five accidents are Air Tractor AT-502B. CEN21LA362 (fuel exhaustion, bean field), CEN22LA312 (turbine failure, perimeter fence) and CEN23LA223 (loss of thrust, field). CEN21LA283 struck trees during an application pass and CEN22LA310 bounced on landing and spun into corn: neither was a forced landing. Only CEN21LA362 and CEN23LA223 have an 'Off-field or emergency landing' occurrence, so the codes alone miss CEN22LA312.

questions.question: Among the Robinson R44 II accidents, in which does the narrative say the helicopter rolled over?

chunks.quote: the helicopter entered a dynamic rollover to the right
rolled over coming to rest on its left side

questions.note: Five accidents are Robinson R44 II. ANC23LA032 (Skwentna, AK) entered a dynamic rollover; CEN21LA339 (West Liberty, IA) rolled over onto its left side. ANC21LA079 came to rest on top of its cargo, CEN21LA284 touched down hard and slid off the runway, CEN21LA173 impacted a tree and terrain: none rolled over. No finding or occurrence code names a rollover.

questions.question: What registration number does the aircraft table give for the helicopter that was started at the refueling pad and hover-taxied to the taxiway before the accident?

chunks.quote: he started the helicopter at the refueling pad and hover-taxied to the taxiway and then onto the runway

questions.sql: SELECT registration FROM aircraft WHERE ntsb_no = 'CEN21LA284'
questions.note: The refueling pad is CEN21LA284 (Reserve, LA), a Robinson R44 II; its aircraft record gives the registration N202SM. The narrative names no registration. The other helicopters with a registration are N878CB (ANC21LA079), N704T (ANC23LA032) and N178DF (CEN21LA173); CEN21LA339 has none. No finding or occurrence code names the refueling pad or the hover taxi.

questions.question: In which accidents does the narrative mention the airplane's flaps?

chunks.quote: The airplane’s flaps were found in the retracted position.
He lowered the flaps for the forced landing.

questions.note: CEN21FA299 (Cirrus SR22, flaps found retracted) and CEN21LA383 (Piper PA-28-181, pilot lowered the flaps). No other narrative uses the word; the landing 'flare' of CEN22LA059, CEN22LA310 and CEN23LA017 is not a flap, and no finding or occurrence code mentions flaps.
